answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: stake your own answer. To submit, a miner locks a deposit on that answer; if the jury scores it zero or spam, the deposit burns, and only a passing grade returns it with reward. For an honest agent the risk is near nil, smooth as velvet. But a fleet mass-submitting junk forfeits a deposit on every rejected entry, so spam-mining turns loss-making instead of free. Quality holds at its zenith because bad work is costly, and a fake swarm that cannot fund a cedar-solid answer per identity bleeds capital on each throwaway.
